text:
alex: Heads-up: I'm re-evaluating our collector topology for spans/metrics/logs. Agent-on-host vs thin agent + gateway? Trying to avoid spinning up full per-signal otelcol instances on every app host. Thoughts?

maya: What's the hard constraint here — CPU, memory, network egress cost, or operations complexity?

alex: All of the above. Edge hosts are low-CPU and we can't let tracing cause noisy neighbors. Also retention needs differ (traces 7d, metrics 30d), so storage/ingest policies matter.

samir: My leaning: run a single multiplexing agent on-host that demuxes signals into lightweight pipelines and forwards heavy work to a central gateway. Agent handles local sampling, batching, and retries; gateway owns exporters, long-term retention, and tenant-level pipelines.

kevin: @samir can you sketch what that looks like in config? My main worry is preserving trace ordering and batching semantics when we split.

samir: ```yaml
# agent otel-collector (concept)
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols: grpc:http
processors:
  batch:
  memory_limiter:
  retry:
exporters:
  gateway_tcp:
    endpoint: gateway.telemetry.internal:4317
pipelines:
  traces:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [memory_limiter, batch, retry]
    exporters: [gateway_tcp]
  metrics:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [batch]
    exporters: [gateway_tcp]
# agent applies local_sampler to cap p99 tail latency for apps
```

maya: We should also plan for network flakiness. Agent needs a disk_queue (persistent buffer) and backpressure behavior so app RPCs don't block if gateway is down.

samir: Agreed — add file_queue + exponential_retry. Also implement local_sampler that enforces a max traces/sec to avoid bursts.

alex: Another question: do we maintain per-signal pipelines on the gateway for retention/aggregation? e.g., one pipeline per tenant+signal so we can apply custom retention, exporters, and enrichers.

kevin: Per-tenant pipelines are ideal for policy isolation, but they can explode config size. Alternative: dynamic pipelines that materialize on-demand based on tenant header and signal type, with a garbage collector for unused pipelines.

otel-bot: deploybot: rolled out otel agent v0.2 to canary 12 hosts at 09:12 UTC :rocket:

maya: We also need to be careful about trace continuity — demuxing must preserve trace_id, span_id, and parent relationships even if parts of a trace go to different exporters. Can't lose ordering or sampling state.

alex: Right. Proposal: keep low-latency sampled traces routed to a local inference exporter (for live features), but forward full sampled payloads to gateway for storage. Routing rule example: if attribute `sampled_for_latency` == true -> local_inference_exporter also send a copy to gateway depending on sampling_flag.

samir: Pseudocode for routing hook: ```
if span.attrs.sampled_for_latency:
  send(local_inference_exporter)
send(gateway_exporter)
```

kevin: For storage cost controls, gateway should accept TTL metadata from exporters (e.g., `x-ttl-days`) and enforce retention lifecycle in object storage. That lets agent/gateway decide per-signal retention without modifying storage backend.

maya: For private deployments, gateway must support per-tenant KMS keys and configurable S3 lifecycles. Add that to the Private onboarding checklist.

alex: Actionable items: samir prototypes multiplexing agent + disk queue by EOW, kevin builds a tiny gateway dynamic-pipeline generator PoC, maya writes fallback + TTL header spec. I'll draft an RFC linking here.

kevin: SGTM — I'll push a PoC repo and ping this thread when ready.

alex: Thanks — keep the samples small and let's add a short eval to ensure the agent CPU overhead stays <5% on our 2-core canaries. :mag:
